internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 1722 occurrences, qwl always presents someone (God, humans, angels, jinn, an ant, a hoopoe, skins, the heavens and earth, Hell) as producing a statement whose content is either quoted directly (the overwhelming pattern: qala/qul/yaqulu + direct quote), pointed back to (qalaha 39:50; qa'iluha 23:100; wa-qilihi 43:88), or held up for evaluation as a content-object (qawl ma'ruf 2:263; asdaq qila 4:122; aqwam qila 73:6; qawluhum bi-afwahihim 9:30; munkar min al-qawl 58:2). The noun qawl/qil names the statement itself; the participle qa'il names its bearer; the passive qila/yuqal backgrounds the sayer while keeping the stated content; Form V taqawwala (52:33, 69:44) adds "manufacture statements from oneself" (fabrication, with al-aqawil as the fabricated statements), leaving the same content-bearing residue. Crucially, the root does NOT require audible vocalization: Yusuf's qala in 12:77 is explicitly kept secret in himself (asarraha fi nafsihi wa-lam yubdiha), and 58:8 has yaquluna fi anfusihim — the saying is internal yet still has quotable content. Conversely, when the Quran wants the physical or faculty layer it uses other roots right next to qwl: ma yalfizu min QAWLIN (50:18 — lafz = emission, qawl = the statement emitted) and the skins' qalu antaqana Allah (41:21 — nutq = granted articulation, qwl = the act of stating). Divine decree uses (haqqa l-qawlu 36:7; 32:13 where the decree's content is quoted in the same verse: la-amla'anna jahannam) and the creative kun (2:117, 16:40, 36:82) are still determinate statements. Even the idiom-like yuqalu lahu Ibrahim (21:60) is a habitual statement whose content is the name. No occurrence uses qwl for mere sound, noise, or contentless expression.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: Form I verb = the event of stating (perfect/imperfect/imperative/jussive); internal passive qila/yuqal = statement with suppressed sayer; masdar qawl/qil = the statement as object; qa'il = statement-bearer; Form V taqawwala = reflexive-appropriative "concoct statements and pin them on another" (self-sourcing is Form V's layer, statement-content is the root's); aqawil = plural of the fabricated statement-object. CONSTRUCTION: qala + direct quote (default quotative frame), qala li- (statement directed at addressee, e.g. 50:30 naqulu li-jahannam), anaphoric object suffix (qalaha). CONTEXT supplies: locus (mouths 9:30 bi-afwahihim vs inner self 12:77, 58:8 fi anfusihim), speaker species (ant 27:18, hoopoe 27:22, skins 41:21, heavens/earth 41:11), authority/efficacy (divine kun 2:117; decree haqqa l-qawlu 36:7), and moral quality (zur 58:2, ma'ruf 2:263, sadid 33:70). After subtracting all of these, the invariant residue — sayer paired with determinate statable content — is non-empty in every occurrence.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 21:60 "yuqalu lahu Ibrahim" (a youth called/named Ibrahim) is the most bleached use — closest to a naming idiom rather than an act of stating. It reconciles because the passive habitual yuqal still frames a recurrent statement whose quoted content is the name itself ("it is said of him: Ibrahim"). Second-strongest pressure: 19:34 "qawla l-haqq" where on one reading qawl designates Jesus himself; on either canonical construal (the true statement about him, or Jesus as realization of God's statement — cf. the kun pattern 2:117, 16:40) the content-individuated-statement residue remains present, so neither case breaks universal presence.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: "qwl = vocal speech / act of speaking aloud." This fails inside the corpus: 12:77 has qala for a statement explicitly concealed and NOT externalized (asarraha fi nafsihi wa-lam yubdiha lahum), and 58:8 has yaquluna fi anfusihim; meanwhile 50:18 (ma yalfizu min qawlin) shows the vocal-emission layer is carried by lfZ, with qawl naming the statement, not the sound. A second competitor, "qwl = authoritative pronouncement/decree," is too narrow: it covers 36:7 and 32:13 but not mundane, false, or fabricated sayings (9:30, 52:33) or polite speech norms (2:263). The content-individuated-statement hypothesis covers all 1722.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from nearest roots via minimal pairs occurring inside this packet's own verses: (1) vs lfZ — 50:18 "ma yalfizu min qawlin": lafz is the physical emission, qawl the statement emitted; (2) vs nTq — 41:21 "qalu antaqana Allah": nutq is the granted faculty of articulation, qwl the exercised act of stating; (3) vs klm — 78:38 "la yatakallamuna illa man adhina lahu r-rahmanu wa-qala sawaban": takallum is engaging in speech at all, qala sawaban is stating evaluably-correct content; likewise 23:100 "kalimatun huwa qa'iluha" pairs kalima (speech-unit) with qa'il (its stater); (4) vs d'w — 24:51: when believers are called (du'u), their qawl is the content-response "sami'na wa-ata'na". Falsifiable: the residue would fail on any occurrence where qwl denoted contentless sound or a non-communicative act; none exists in the full set.
internal_discovery.rationale: Full coverage was achieved programmatically: every one of the 1722 packet occurrences was token-extracted from its cited verse text (with basmala offset correction) and classified into exhaustive morphological clusters (906 + 355 + 259 + 43 + 9 + 52 passive + 92 qawl-noun + 4 qil + 5 qa'il + 1 aqawil + 2 Form V = 1722, matching the packet inventory N=102/V=1618/V(V)=2); every cluster and every detected anomaly (non-human sayers 27:18, 27:22, 41:11, 41:21, 50:30; internal saying 12:77, 58:8; decree/creative uses 2:117, 16:40, 32:13, 36:7, 36:82, 38:84; naming 21:60; anaphoric 39:50, 23:100, 43:88; fabrication 52:33, 69:44; negated 20:89; evaluative nouns 4:122, 56:26, 73:6, 2:263, 9:30, 50:18) was read in full verse context. The proposed residue — sayer paired with determinate, quotable/evaluable statement-content — survives subtraction of form, construction, and context in every occurrence, is non-empty, and is distinguished from lfZ, nTq, klm, and d'w by minimal pairs within the packet's own verses. No occurrence required forcing; universal presence holds without exception, so the result is PREFERRED at STRONG rather than UNRESOLVED.

adversarial_verification.notes: Full coverage of 1722 occurrences clustered by form: V(1618) verbal 'say' (incl. passive qīla, which still issues a determinate utterance with content present, sayer demoted); N(102) qawl/qīl/qāʾil reviewed ref-by-ref; V(V)(2) taqawwala/al-aqāwīl (52:33, 69:44) = fabricated but content-individuated sayings. Every candidate-resistant cluster reconciles: (a) ḥaqqa/waqaʿa al-qawl 'decree' group (17:16,27:82,27:85,28:63,32:13,36:7,36:70,37:31,41:25,46:18) is decisively content — 32:13 quotes the decree verbatim ('laʾamlaʾanna jahannama…'); (b) metaphorical sayers (heavens 41:11, ant 27:18, skins 41:21) and Jesus-as-qawl al-ḥaqq (19:34) retain the 'statable statement' residue under metaphor; (c) Quran-as-qawl of messenger/human/poet/kāhin/šayṭān (69:40-42, 74:25, 81:19, 81:25, 86:13) = product-of-a-sayer with referenceable content (covers the 'issuer/product' clause). No pure-address (qāla li- always takes following content), no pure-vocalization, no faculty-of-articulation use. Distinctiveness is confirmed by INTERNAL minimal contrasts where the excluded dimensions are lexicalized separately ALONGSIDE qwl: lafẓ vs qawl (50:18), jahr vs qawl (20:7, 21:110), bi-afwāhikum/bi-alsinatihim vs qawl (33:4, 3:167, 48:11) — leaving qwl = pairing of sayer with statable content, distinct from nṭq (faculty), lfẓ/ṣwt (vocalization), ndy/dʿw (address). Falsifiable via any qwl lacking statable/quotable/referenceable content; none exists. Under non-negotiable root unity, no unreconciled confirmed occurrence found; the adversarial refutation attempt failed.
